Every GPU and NPU output is checked; wake = CNTVCT at the interrupt handler entry to the waiting task's return, both devices on CNTVCT. PLL watch: 42-52 PLL_GPU0 writes seen, at least 21 with an NPU job in flight, PLL_NPU word unchanged and LOCK set at every read before, after and at the next NPU completion. conclusion: The GPU, the NPU and five CPU streaming workers ran together in one returning image and returned normally with both retirement receipts valid (GPU off, worker parked; NPU stopped, no mismatch). Every GPU and NPU output equalled its reference, PLL_NPU kept 0xf9104600 with LOCK set through 52 PLL_GPU0 writes (42 with an NPU job in flight) and 31 completion reads, and no phase throttled. Every wake maximum is far inside its 1,000 us budget: 17.0 us GPU and 10.0 us NPU under streaming. Eleven predictions missed: the wake p50, p99 and maximum ranges were too high (the measured spreads are about 1 us alone), the GPU p50 rise under streaming was 4.0 us (predicted 0.5-3), and streaming cut the GPU job rate by 63% and the NPU rate by 54% (predicted 0-15% and 5-30%), so DRAM contention from 6.5 GB/s of streaming, not CPU wake latency, limits the accelerators under load. The run total was 52 s against 86-109 s.
